canine.source: 2019 AAHA Canine Life Stage Guidelines — TABLE 1

stages.label: Puppy
stages.definition_verbatim: Birth to cessation of rapid growth (~6-9 mo, varying with breed and size)

stages.label: Young adult
stages.definition_verbatim: Cessation of rapid growth to completion of physical and social maturation, which occurs in most dogs by 3 to 4 yr of age

stages.label: Mature adult
stages.definition_verbatim: Completion of physical and social maturation until the last 25% of estimated lifespan (breed and size dependent)

stages.label: Senior
stages.definition_verbatim: The last 25% of estimated lifespan through end of life

stages.label: End of life
stages.definition_verbatim: Terminal stage (depends on the specific pathologies)

visit_frequency_notes: Puppies: frequent visits per vaccination / socialization needs
Young adults: semiannual to annual consultation and physical exam
Mature adults: semiannual-to-annual exams; annual minimum database (Table 4)
Seniors: at least semiannual exams and minimum database (Table 4)

feline.source: 2021 AAHA/AAFP Feline Life Stage Guidelines — TABLE 1 / summary

stages.label: End of life
stages.definition_verbatim: Separate stage; see 2016 AAHA/IAAHPC EOL Guidelines and 2021 AAFP End of Life toolkit (not expanded here)

visit_frequency_notes: Senior cats should be seen at least every 6 months (and more often as needed)
